title: The Beginning of Metaphysical Questioning with the Question of World. The Path of the Investigation and Its Difficulties

work.full: The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics: World, Finitude, Solitude

spine_role: Closing unit of the boredom spine's Part-Two hinge: opens the world-question comparatively, states the methodological difficulty of access to 'life', and (§44) recapitulates the whole boredom→questions arc after the vacation, restating the attunement-grounding of metaphysical questioning in compact form.

section_map.heading: The path of a comparative examination of three guiding theses: the stone is worldless, the animal is poor in world, man is world-forming
section_map.gist: Three paths to 'What is world?': (1) the historical/etymological path of On the Essence of Ground (kosmos / mundus / world); (2) the everyday-world path of Being and Time (departure from the ready-to-hand); (3) the chosen third path, a comparative examination of stone, animal, and man, formulated in the three guiding theses. Each path comes 'from without' and carries ordinary understanding's perspectives, which must be transformed; metaphysics is prior to the beneficial/inimical-to-culture distinction and so is 'ambiguous'.

section_map.heading: The fundamental difficulty with respect to content and method in determining the essence and accessibility of life
section_map.gist: Even the man/animal distinction (rational vs non-rational living being) is hard to fix; the real question is what 'reason' means and whether that distinction is the metaphysically essential one. Two difficulties: [1] content — what is the essence of life as such?; [2] method — by what path is the living character of the living being originarily accessible (if at all)? The animal can neither observe nor report itself; we must interpret its expression. Hence we move in a circle — the mark of philosophy; dizziness before the question is the price of entering the circle at all.

section_map.heading: Summary and renewed introduction following the vacation: metaphysics as comprehensive questioning; awakening the fundamental attunement of profound boredom; the metaphysical questions to be developed from the fundamental attunement. Guidelines for correctly understanding this talk about the fundamental attunement of philosophizing
section_map.gist: Recapitulation after the semester break. Metaphysics is comprehensive questioning in a twofold sense: beings as a whole are included in every metaphysical question, and the questioner is caught up in and affected by the questioning. Being affected presupposes being attuned; only an attuned being can be adversely/otherwise attuned, hence can undergo a change of attunement — and so an attunement can be awakened. Part One's interpretation of profound boredom in the ground of Dasein was dedicated to awakening such a fundamental attunement and creating the possibility of being gripped. From it the three questions are developed: [1] What is world? [2] What is finitude? [3] What is individuation? — the second being the most originary and central. Seven guidelines correct the talk of a fundamental attunement of philosophizing (questions are drawn from, not exhausting; not the only path; chosen yet bound/compelled; the choice binds us to metaphysics' finite-Dasein-compelling character; every genuine attunement liberates and deepens the others; rooted in the history of Dasein, not calculable; philosophy as creative stands in the fundamental attunement of melancholy — with the Aristotle Problemata XXX.1 melancholy-of-exceptional-men citation). Closes by re-listing the three paths and the three theses.

objects.name: What is world?
objects.note: First of the three metaphysical questions; the explicit theme of all of Part Two.

objects.name: What is finitude?
objects.note: Second and, per §44, 'the most originary and most central' of the three questions.

objects.name: What is individuation?
objects.note: Third of the three questions developed from profound boredom.

objects.name: The stone is worldless
objects.note: Thesis [1]; the material object has no world; lower limit of the comparison.

objects.name: The animal is poor in world
objects.note: Thesis [2]; the 'intermediate thesis' from which the comparative examination will begin (Ch.3). Poverty = deprivation, not lesser quantity.

objects.name: Man is world-forming
objects.note: Thesis [3]; upper limit; man not merely part of world but 'master and servant' of world, 'having' world.

objects.name: fundamental attunement
objects.note: What must be awakened so comprehensive questioning is possible; disclosive, not subjective coloring. Only an attuned being can be otherwise-attuned, hence awakened.

objects.name: profound boredom
objects.note: The specific fundamental attunement interpreted in Part One ('a profound boredom in the ground of our Dasein'); the ground from which the three questions are drawn.

objects.name: melancholy
objects.note: Guideline [7]: philosophy as creative human activity stands in the fundamental attunement of melancholy; concerns the form, not the content, of philosophizing; rooted in Mut/Gemüt word-family.

objects.name: comprehensive questioning
objects.note: Metaphysics' twofold structure: beings-as-a-whole included; the questioner caught up and affected.

objects.name: comparative examination
objects.note: The third path; sets stone/animal/man in relief by their differing relation to world.

objects.name: being-gripped / being affected
objects.note: The possibility of being gripped belongs to the essence of man insofar as Da-sein implies being attuned; awakening attunement creates this possibility.

objects.name: the circle of philosophy
objects.note: Constant circling = mark of moving within philosophy; dizziness/the uncanny, 'suspended in the Nothing'; insight into the centre is possible only in circling.

objects.name: having-world
objects.note: Man's standing-over-against the world: master and servant, that in which he moves — the phenomenon that opens the comparative question about animals/stone.

objects.name: kosmos
objects.note: kosmos / mundus / 'world' — the conceptual history sketched in On the Essence of Ground, §II.

objects.name: Mut / Gemüt / Schwermut / Armut
objects.note: Translator's note: older sense of Mut = 'cheer/spirits/mood'; Schwermut = melancholy; Gemüt = 'overall mood'; the root Mut anchors the animal's 'poverty' (Armut) in §46.

objects.name: Aristotle
objects.note: Problemata XXX.1 (953a10ff., Bekker): why are all exceptional men — in philosophy, politics, poetry, the arts — melancholics? Empedocles, Socrates, Plato named; melancholy dia physin vs dia noson.

objects.name: Novalis (implicit) / On the Essence of Ground / Being and Time
objects.note: Heidegger's own prior works invoked as the first two paths: Vom Wesen des Grundes (history of 'world') and Sein und Zeit (everyday phenomenon of world).

objects.name: metaphysics is prior to the culture-distinction
objects.note: Metaphysics cannot be assessed by ordinary understanding's criteria; neither beneficial nor inimical to culture, or both at once — 'ambiguous' because basically prior to such distinctions.

objects.name: every genuine fundamental attunement liberates and deepens the others
objects.note: Guideline [5]; attunements are not interchangeable items on one level; experienced only through Dasein, not via a psychology of feelings.

bridge_relevance: §44 is the most compact restatement in FCM of the boredom→questions spine that the King-Salvo bridge depends on: profound boredom, interpreted to its ground, is what releases the metaphysical questions. The unit anchors why the empirical pipeline's boredom stimulus is treated as more than a feeling-state — boredom is an attunement to be awakened/interpreted, paralleling the pipeline's move from a 'psychology of feelings' (which Heidegger here explicitly rejects, p.182) toward EEG/gaze/phenomenological triangulation of an attunement. The three-thesis comparative frame (stone/animal/man, by relation to world) and the form-not-content claim about melancholy supply structural vocabulary for the bridge's surface/depth split.
